rows.b: Rows of beads on rods are slid by hand to add, subtract, multiply, and divide. Each column stands for a place value, so the beads remember the running total.
A chip designed for one thing: the matrix math that AI runs on. It does in seconds what would take a regular processor hours.
A future processor where magnetic spins do the logic with no charge current at all, promising instant-on computers that sip power. SPECULATION: spin logic is still laboratory research.
A kit computer with toggle switches on the front and no keyboard or screen at first. Hobbyists flipped in programs bit by bit and watched the lights answer.
A machine with custom chips for graphics and sound that could do animation and stereo music years ahead of rivals. Video producers used it for titling and effects.
Analog circuits integrate and differentiate continuously while a digital side sets up the problem and reads the answer. Old hybrids simulated aircraft and rockets this way.
A design with a mill for arithmetic, a store for memory, and punched cards to direct the sequence of operations — the same three parts a modern computer has. Programs could branch and loop.
A box of bronze gears that predicted the positions of the sun and moon, the dates of eclipses, and the cycles of the ancient games. Turning one crank moved pointers across dials on both faces.
A bare circuit board sold without case, keyboard, or power supply — the buyer finished the computer. It displayed text on an ordinary television.
A home computer with color graphics, sound, and slots for expansion cards. It ran the first spreadsheet program, which gave businesses a reason to buy it.
A Mac where the processor, graphics, and memory live on one efficient chip. It runs cool and quiet while beating older multi-chip designs.
A single chip holding the processor, graphics, radio, and memory controller for a phone. It sips power so the battery lasts all day while running demanding apps.
A sixteen-bit machine with a crisp monochrome display option and built-in MIDI ports that made it the studio standard for musicians. It brought real power to a home price.
Dozens of small rugged computers inside a car manage the engine, brakes, and airbags. They must never crash, so they are built to extreme reliability standards.
